text: A municipal water utility's open-channel grit removal basin at a 40-megalitre-per-day plant loses fine-grit capture every storm event: grit smaller than 300 micrometres passes the 12-metre-long settling channel during peak wet-weather flow of 900 litres per second, and downstream pump impellers lose 30 percent of their rated head within 18 months as captured fines abrade the vanes. The channel operates at 1.4-metre depth with a 0.6-metre-per-second peak velocity and the operators must hold grit capture above 85 percent for particles down to 200 micrometres across the full storm hydrograph, without basin volume expansion (the site boundary is fixed), without polymer or coagulant dosing (no chemical storage permits available), and without powered screens (the plant has no spare electrical capacity).
